messages:
marta: Quick brain dump — running into an operator coordination edge with airgapped deliveries where local node caches act as a peer-cache layer. If node A finishes fetching a component and node B starts simultaneously we get duplicate pulls and weird activation races. want thoughts on guardrails.

sam: Could we use a short-lived lease per blob + CAS id? node that wins lease serves peers for Xs, others wait. simple and avoids double work.

jen: Lease sounds ok but we need to account for disconnected nodes where the lease-holder goes offline mid-transfer. fallback plan?

marta: Good call. Proposal: lease + resumable transfer tokens anchored to signed manifest. tokens expire, operator can force a handoff if holder disappears after T_backoff.

kevin: How do we detect holder disappearance reliably in airgapped envs? heartbeats to local operator? network partitions make fast decisions risky.

sam: Operator should be conservative: after lease TTL + grace, other nodes try optimistic fetch from alternate peers or from operator fallback (local repo). Add a small randomized jitter before failover to avoid thundering herd.

jen: Also need integrity: peers should verify component sigs and SHA256 before committing to activation. Add a verification stage separate from lease ownership, so a bad holder can't trick others.

marta: Agreed. Workflow sketch: 1) node requests blob; 2) operator grants lease (holder id + TTL) or returns peer list; 3) holder caches and serves; 4) requesters verify sig+sha before apply; 5) if holder missing after TTL+grace operator triggers fallback and increments failure counter for telemetry.

kevin: Can we avoid centralized operator when possible? maybe let nodes elect a temporary 'serving leader' via gossip if operator unreachable. leader selection simple: lowest node-id among observers with blob present. fallback to operator only if quorum missing.

jen: Gossip adds complexity but could be optional mode. Documented config: "peer_serve_mode": ["operator_lease", "gossip_leader"], default operator_lease.

marta: Nice. Also want to limit memory pressure: serve only up to N concurrent streams per holder, queue others. config knob `max_peer_streams` + `stream_backpressure_ms`.

sam: Telemetry: emit events for lease_granted, lease_expired, peer_handoff, verify_failed. That will let us tune TTL/backoff.

marta: Final question: do we accept partial blob serving (chunked) or require whole object? chunked helps resume but increases attack surface. thoughts?

kevin: Chunked is useful for large model shards. enforce chunk signatures (per-chunk hash chain) so partial data is verifiable. otherwise whole-object only.

jen: Implementation notes: add API on operator: POST /lease {blob, requestor} -> {holder, ttl} and POST /handoff {blob, new_holder} authorized by operator. Nodes need simple in-memory lease cache and persistent resume tokens.

marta: Thanks — I'll draft an RFC with these patterns: operator-lease default, optional gossip leader, resumable chunked transfers with per-chunk verification, lease TTL/grace + jittered failover, telemetry hooks. Will drop a rough design doc in #architecture tomorrow. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed: added reminder to calendar for RFC review meeting on Mon 10am.
